title: CCNB1IP1 regulatory evolution underlies gradual increases in cortical size and folding in primates.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Found the data statement in the open bioRxiv/PMC preprint (PMC11661109) of this paper: all sequencing data are in GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series GSE247966. Pulled GEO metadata: GSE247966 = 12 Chinese tree shrew fetal cortex RNA-seq samples (3 embryos x 4 cortical layers: VZ, ISVZ, OSVZ, CP); it is a sub-series of GSE247971, whose only other sub-series GSE203351 is 6 human SH-SY5Y cell samples (CCNB1IP1-overexpression vs GFP control). Downloaded and opened two per-sample processed files (GSM7903881 cortical plate, GSM7903884 ventricular zone, ~1.8 MB each gzipped): Cufflinks output with 81,792 gene rows and columns tracking_id, gene_short_name, locus, FPKM, FPKM_conf_lo/hi, FPKM_status. Total deposited samples across the whole study: 18.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The cross-species comparison (CCNB1IP1 expression vs divergence time R=0.84, vs brain weight R=0.91, vs gyrification index R=0.94), the luciferase reporter assays on two cis-regulatory elements (CRE1, CRE2) in human and chimpanzee plus five deletion constructs, the mouse knock-in phenotyping, and the 20-mammal protein alignment are described in the preprint text and figures only; none of those numbers are deposited as a data table I could open. The published Nature Genetics version is paywalled and not in PubMed Central, so I could not read its final data-availability statement or supplementary tables.
verified.note: Europe PMC reports no open access, no PMC copy, no supplementary files and no text-mined accessions for the Nature Genetics record; NCBI elink from PMID 42811076 returns no GEO/BioProject links yet. The GEO accession came from the preprint.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO GSE247966/GSE247971 are public, no login. I downloaded two processed FPKM (fragments per kilobase of transcript per million mapped reads) files directly from the NCBI FTP site.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target is a column anywhere in the deposited files. The only quantities worth predicting - each primate species' gyrification index (how folded its cortex is) and brain weight - appear only in the paper's figures, and would have to be assembled by hand from the literature and joined to expression values taken from other published datasets. The deposited files contain gene expression only, with layer and embryo encoded in file names.

a3_inputs_present.note: Expression values and genomic loci are in the files (81,792 rows per sample, tree shrew gene IDs plus human-style gene symbols); nothing needs a bulk accession lookup.

a4_units_stated.note: Column header states FPKM with confidence bounds and a status flag; verified in the opened file.

a5_enough_rows.note: The modelling unit is the sample or the species, not the gene. 12 tree shrew cortex samples plus 6 human cell-line samples = 18 total, and the cross-species trait analysis covers roughly a dozen primates. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows (400 for classification). This is two orders of magnitude short.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially laptop-sized; the whole series tar is 21 MB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO's 12 tree shrew samples match the preprint's described design (E35 cortex, four laminae, three embryos); 6 human samples match the overexpression experiment.

a8_label_provenance.note: FPKM values are real RNA-seq measurements, not another model's output - but there is no label to trace, which is the A2 failure above.

existing_models.name: Enformer (Avsec et al., Nature Methods 2021), a deep neural network that predicts gene expression and chromatin signal from ~200 kb of DNA sequence
existing_models.score_and_split: Retrieved its Nature Methods record via web search; it is trained jointly on human and mouse genomes and evaluated on held-out genomic regions. I did not retrieve a number for any primate cortical-folding task, because none exists.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved in full text; the widely discussed open problem in this family of models is predicting expression differences between individuals or species rather than between genomic loci.

c2_audit.note: Searched for sequence-to-expression models in primate brain. Nothing models this paper's specific question (species cortical folding from cortical expression), but that is because there is no dataset of a usable size, not because the field is empty.

backbone.name: none applicable at this scale
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop would suffice, but 18 samples cannot train or honestly evaluate a head
backbone.licence: GEO data are unrestricted public domain

integration.partner_dataset: Primate brain MRI trait compilations (gyrification index, brain weight) and multi-species cortex RNA-seq atlases
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which genes' cortical expression tracks cortical folding across mammals? - a real question, but it needs tens to hundreds of species, and this paper contributes one outgroup species.

controls.positive_control: Cortical layer identity (VZ/ISVZ/OSVZ/CP) is recoverable from the expression tables and known marker genes should separate them - but with 12 samples this is a sanity check, not a project.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is possible in principle; with n=12 it is uninformative.
controls.external_validation: Human and macaque fetal cortex lamina RNA-seq (GEO GSE38805, cited in the methods) exists as an independent source, but again at sample scale, not row scale.

honest_claim_h3: With 18 deposited RNA-seq samples and a species-level trait table that exists only in figures, any model here would claim at most 'cortical layer identity is predictable from expression in three tree shrew embryos', which nobody needs.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use cortical gene expression across primate species to predict how large and folded that species' cortex is.
plain_idea.train_on: One expression profile per species' developing cortex. Verified availability: 12 tree shrew cortical-layer samples and 6 human cell-line samples, 18 in total; the multi-species panel the paper correlates against is not deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Gyrification index (a ratio measuring how folded a cortex is, from brain surface tracing) and brain weight per species, both measured by anatomists and reported in earlier literature, not in this paper's files.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Comparative neuroanatomists and brain-evolution labs would like a ranked list of genes whose expression tracks cortical folding; even a failed model would say expression alone cannot explain the trait. It is not doable at this sample size.

more_or_better_data.why: 18 samples from one lab, one new species, one developmental stage. Enformer and its successors were trained on thousands of genome-wide tracks.

confidence_score.why: Three biological replicates per layer in one species gives a noise estimate for those 12 samples only, not calibrated uncertainty for any prediction task.

models_beatable.why: There is no competing model on this task to beat, and no data to build one; the comparison is vacuous.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No existing model can be run as a baseline on these 18 samples, so the first condition fails immediately.

ml_idea: The only well-posed task the deposited data supports is classifying cortical germinal-layer identity (ventricular zone, inner and outer subventricular zone, cortical plate) from gene expression, with 12 samples - far too few. The attractive task, predicting cortical folding from cross-species cortical expression, has no deposited label table and only around a dozen species.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the two files I opened: 81,792 rows x 18 samples of Cufflinks output is a few tens of megabytes in memory as a pandas table. No timing run was needed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited samples in GEO before anything else - 12 tree shrew plus 6 human cell-line = 18. That number alone ends the project, and it takes one page load.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A on two killers, both verified in the files rather than inferred from the abstract. A2: the only interesting labels (gyrification index, brain weight per primate species) are not columns in any deposited file and would have to be assembled from the literature and other papers' expression datasets. A5: the entire study deposits 18 RNA-seq samples (12 tree shrew cortical-layer, 6 human cell-line), against a threshold of roughly 1,500 labelled rows. This is a careful single-gene evolutionary and functional study - mouse knock-ins, luciferase reporters, immunostaining - whose value is mechanistic, not statistical. There is no machine-learning project here at any size.
